title: Meltwater Pulse 1A
summary: Meltwater Pulse 1A was an abrupt jump in global sea level during the last deglaciation. Tahiti corals bracket it between 14,650 and 14,310 years ago, with a rise there of 12 to 22 metres, most probably 14 to 18, in step with the Bølling warming. Which ice sheets supplied the water is still argued: Southern Hemisphere and North American sources have both been proposed.

uncertainty.note: The paper counts years before AD 1950, so 14,650 and 14,310 years ago become astronomical years -12700 and -12360. The record id (-14600) uses the rounded years-ago figure directly.

as_recorded.value: MWP-1A started no earlier than 14,650 years ago and ended before 14,310 years ago

where.modern_name: Tahiti, French Polynesia (coral drilling site offshore; the event itself was global)
where.historical_name: No single place: a global sea-level rise recorded offshore of Tahiti

importance.justification: The most extreme deglacial sea-level jump on record, used to test how fast ice sheets can lose mass.

sources.title: Ice-sheet collapse and sea-level rise at the Bølling warming 14,600 years ago (Nature 483:559–564, doi:10.1038/nature10902)
sources.publisher: Nature (Springer Nature); PDF hosted by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
sources.author: Pierre Deschamps, Nicolas Durand, Edouard Bard, et al.

sources.title: Saddle collapse behind rapid sea level rise

reviewer_note: Least sure of the record id: -14600 treats 14,600 years ago as a calendar year, while the sourced dates count from AD 1950 and give about -12700 to -12360. The pin is the Tahiti coral site only as a marker; uncertainty_km is 5000 because the event is global. The ice-sheet source is contested and is stated as such; the North American model result (a rise of 9 metres in 500 years) comes from a news summary of one study.
